title: Council limits its own debate to three minutes
tagline: Before Cox Ranch gets its second reading, the council writes a rule about how long it may talk about it.
logline: Two annexation hearings, three long-postponed Cox Ranch ordinances, a speaking-time limit for the dais, a truck-weight resolution that fails, and a Comprehensive Plan contract that passes without a single no.

moments.text: On the BOPU parcel bundled into the Cox annexation: “we can annex anytime we want” — it was bundled to save survey cost.

Said DEQ and “19 agencies” vet data centers before a permit. Mr. Wolfe answered on the record that DEQ regulates backup-generator air permits and stormwater, not wildlife or water use, and is not Industrial Siting.
Aldrich: the Sherard plant discharge is roughly 150 acre-feet a year. Mayor: data centers used 95 million of 7.17 billion gallons last year (1.3%).
350–500 full-time jobs across three shifts; no lease with King Ranch — “verbal conversations” only; “Commitment to Cheyenne” not yet in writing; an Austin site uses about 124,000 gallons a year.
Offered a 500+ foot buffer plus noise and zero-spill lighting “as a binding condition… in writing” and a Wallick/Parsley road expansion; confirmed a data center as the use.
Orchard Hills notice: mailed Aug 13, deadline Aug 14, receipt Aug 17. Staff frames compliance on the mailing date.
Will produce a “% of Cheyenne annexed for data centers” figure for PSC on Sept 21.
Construction-phase lighting is exempt from the lighting ordinance; enforcement is by complaint or voluntary.
I-25/College diverging diamond needs two more lanes; timing is “in WYDOT’s hands”; a traffic study was submitted.
Laybourn: the Comp Plan is “not routine” and asked why the update lapsed after 2014. Bloom: funding was requested for FY2020 and FY2025 but not granted.

layman.headline: The council voted 6–3 to move three Cox Ranch ordinances past their second reading — after first voting to cap its own members at three minutes per item.
brief: Think of Monday night as a season episode with one big plot and several side stories. The big plot: a very large piece of land west of town (Cox Ranch, about 1,260 acres) has been waiting since April to be added to the city. On Monday, the council passed the second of three required readings, 6–3. Mr. Laybourn, Mr. Moody and Mr. Wolfe voted no.

Side story one: before that, Dr. Aldrich moved to limit each council member to one speech of three minutes per item. It passed over objections from the same three members. It applies to the council, not to residents who sign up to speak.

Side story two: two more annexation hearings (Orchard Hills and Hitching Post, together about 815 acres) were held and closed with no vote. Both are headed to the Public Services Committee on Sept 21. A resolution opposing heavier trucks on national highways failed. A $351,790 contract for a new Comprehensive Plan passed with no opposition.
deep: Annexation means the city draws its boundary around new land, so city services and city rules apply there. In Wyoming the council must hold a hearing and make findings first (W.S. §15-1-402). It also reads each ordinance three times, usually with a committee in between. Cox Ranch got its first reading Apr 13 and a second reading date of Apr 27, when the council postponed it to Sept 14. That postponement is why Monday felt like a return, not a premiere.

The land in question touches the city boundary along only about 5.26% of its edge, according to the staff report, which says the small percentage is due to the size of the annexation. Wyoming’s statute asks that the land be contiguous with or adjacent to the city, not that a set percentage touches it. That is why contiguity shows up as a flag in the watchdog’s rule engine but is not itself an illegality.

Several statements at the podium came from sources that are not yet in the official minutes (see the “moments to verify” list), including the Mayor’s comments on water use and the developers’ verbal commitments. The lenses label which facts come from the official record and which come from the watchdog’s notes.

What happens next: the Orchard Hills and Hitching Post items go through committee on Sept 21 and return to council on Sept 28. A third reading for Cox Ranch remains. The sources disagree on when (the PSC Sept 21 packet labels it a 3rd reading, the watchdog timeline says Oct 12), so this is marked unresolved.
layman.kids: A big piece of land wants to join the city. The council has to vote three times before it can. On Monday it voted the second time, and most members said yes. Before they started, they agreed that council members would each get only three minutes to talk about each topic.

legal.disclaimer: Educational analysis built from the agenda packet and cited statutes. Not legal advice; verify statutory text at wyoleg.gov and the final minutes.

issues.question: What must the governing body find before land can be annexed?
issues.rule: W.S. §15-1-402 requires findings at a §15-1-405 hearing, including that annexation protects the health, safety and welfare of residents of the area and the city; that the area is a logical and feasible addition with services reasonably available; and that it is contiguous with or adjacent to the city or meets §15-1-407. Contiguity is not defeated by a platted street, right-of-way or waterway.
issues.application: Items 6a and 6b were the §15-1-402 compliance hearings. The Cox packet reports 5.26% contiguity and says the percentage is small because of the annexation’s size.
issues.conclusion: The text sets no percentage floor; adjacency suffices. The 35% line in the watchdog rule engine is a pattern flag, not a legal threshold. Whether the findings are supported is a matter for the record, not for a percentage.
cites: In re West Laramie, 457 P.2d 498 (Wyo. 1969) (as annotated: contiguity is the only scope requirement)

issues.question: Was the Orchard Hills notice timely?
issues.rule: The annexing city must have “sent by certified mail” to landowners and affected utilities a summary of the annexation report not less than twenty (20) business days before the hearing (W.S. §15-1-402).
issues.application: Hearing: Mon Sept 14, 2026. Counting back 20 business days and skipping Labor Day (Sept 7), day 20 is Fri Aug 14. Per staff: mailed Aug 13, receipt Aug 17.
issues.conclusion: The verb in the statute is “sent”, which supports staff’s choice of the mailing date. The Hitching Post packet mentions a delivery confirmation dated “August 18, 2025” — flagged by the rule engine as a year mix, probably a typo for 2026.

issues.question: Can the council cap its own members’ debate?
issues.rule: Deliberative bodies may adopt a motion limiting the length or number of speeches. The mover cited Robert’s Rules; staff said the limit binds the governing body only.
issues.application: Adopted on Dr. Aldrich’s motion; Wolfe, Moody and Laybourn voted no.
issues.conclusion: A procedural choice within the body’s own rules. Public-comment rules are separate and unaffected per staff’s clarification.
cites: Robert’s Rules of Order (as cited by the mover in the debrief)

issues.question: Is Cox Ranch finished?
issues.rule: Ordinances pass after three readings; each reading is a separate vote.
issues.application: Second reading passed 6–3. The ordinance record shows first reading Apr 13, second Apr 27 (postponed), second again Sept 14.
issues.conclusion: Not final. Sources disagree on timing of the third reading (PSC Sept 21 packet labels item 7 “3rd READING”; the watchdog timeline says Oct 12). Marked unresolved.

issues.question: Can the council overrule the Planning Commission?
issues.rule: The agenda includes a resolution “overruling the Planning Commission’s denial” of PUDC-26-176, a Future Land Use Map change (item 23).
issues.application: Referred to PSC, so no decision yet. The watchdog notes say the council overruled a Planning Commission denial 7–3 on July 13.
issues.conclusion: Precedent exists in this season; the next step is committee.

script.text: INT. CHEYENNE MUNICIPAL BUILDING — COUNCIL CHAMBERS — MONDAY, SEPT. 14, 2026 — 6:00 P.M.
The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne convenes (agenda items 1–3: call to order, roll, pledge). MAYOR PATRICK COLLINS presides. CITY CLERK KYLIE SODEN keeps the record.
DR. ALDRICH moves a limit on debate: three minutes, one speech, council members only. WOLFE, MOODY and LAYBOURN object. The motion carries.
Two public hearings under W.S. §15-1-402: 162.42 acres (Orchard Hills) and 652.67 acres (Hitching Post). Both are closed without a vote.
Notice was mailed Aug 13; the deadline was Aug 14; receipt was Aug 17.
Three ordinances, three votes, one result each: 6–3. LAYBOURN, MOODY and WOLFE vote no. DR. RINNE is not yet in the room.
Seven first readings go to the Public Services Committee. A resolution opposing heavier trucks fails. A $351,790 plan contract passes with no opposition.

themeLyrics: Second and fourth Monday at six,
Gavel comes down and the agenda picks up its sticks.
Read it once, read it twice, read it three,
Every vote on the record for the whole city to see.
Zones and streets and a line on a map,
Somebody asks, somebody answers, somebody’s on the clock.
This is the Real Windy City —
Tonight’s episode, coming up after the roll call!
